claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your responsibility for Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, are you paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after him - for example on food, clothes or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me - he lives elsewhere. But I do help out with his upkeep. I contribute money towards his needs each week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is important for determining your eligibility.

**How much do you contribute weekly towards Alex's upkeep, and what does this cover (for example, food, clothes, pocket money, or contributions to his accommodation)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £10 a week towards Alex's upkeep. I help out with things like clothes and other bits and pieces he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I need to clarify one more important detail:

**Who does Alex currently live with? Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure if anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for him at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me gather one final piece of information to complete my assessment:

**The current Child Benefit rate is £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child. You mentioned you contribute £10 per week. To qualify for Child Benefit when your child lives elsewhere, you need to contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment (or equivalent in kind) towards their upkeep. Are you able to increase your contributions to at least match the Child Benefit rate, or are there other contributions you're making that we haven't counted yet?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, £10 a week is what I'm able to contribute at the moment. That's all I'm giving towards his upkeep right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you would **not be eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

While Alex meets the age requirement (he's 8 years old, which is under 16) and you live in the UK, the issue is with the responsibility criteria. Since Alex doesn't live with you, you would need to contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment towards his upkeep to qualify. 

The current Child Benefit rate is £25.60 per week for an eldest or only child. You're currently contributing £10 per week, which unfortunately falls short of the required amount.

**Your options:**

1. If you're able to increase your contributions to at least £25.60 per week (or the equivalent in kind through clothes, food, pocket money, etc.), you could potentially become eligible.

2. If someone else is living with Alex and providing for his day-to-day care, they may be able to claim Child Benefit instead (only one person can claim for each child).

If you have any questions about this decision or if your circumstances change, you can contact the Child Benefit Office for further guidance.
